newsitem.title: CANADA: Cricket-Pakistan level series in a thriller.
newsitem.headline: Cricket-Pakistan level series in a thriller.

text.p: Former captain Salim Malik hit a boundary from the second last ball of the day to snatch a two wicket victory for Pakistan in the second match of the Sahara Cup cricket series against India in Toronto on Tuesday.

Malik's 70 not out earned him the player of the match award and lifted Pakistan to 266-8 off 49.5 overs in reply to India's 264-6 off a maximum 50 overs at the Toronto Cricket, Skating and Curling Club.
The 33-year-old right hander held the innings together as India's bowlers, led by leg spinner Anil Kumble (one for 32 off ten overs) and opener Javagal Srinath (two for 53), started to get on top.

Malik got match winning support from tailender Saqlain Mushtaq (11 no), the pair constructing an undefeated 45 run stand for the ninth wicket to get Pakistan home and level the five-match series at 1-1.

India had set the Pakistanis a tough challenge with promising Rahul Dravid (90) and veteran Mohammad Azharuddin (88) piling on 161 runs, an Indian record for a third wicket stand in limited overs internationals.
The Toronto wicket, which was under cover all weekend as rain soaked the Canadian city, generally played truly, allowing the talented Indian lineup to punish the Pakistan opening attack.

In the run chase, Pakistan lost an early wicket, Aamir Sohail caught behind without scoring when the score was 10, but his left hand partner Saeed Anwar attacked relentlessly and put his team in the picture.
The dashing 28-year-old smashed six boundaries and three sixes in his innings of 80 off just 78 balls.

He got good support from Inzamam-ul-Haq (29), but India stuck to the task and eventually looked in control of the match when Mushtaq Ahmed was dismissed, leaving Pakistan 221-8 with more than eight overs to be bowled.

However, Saqlain gave Malik the support he needed, picking up singles to give the senior player the strike at vital times and making it possible for Pakistan to thrill the boisterous crowd with a last-gasp victory.
